site.sitedescription: Degraded lower montane forest occupies the steep slopes and ridges above about 1800 m. Nothofagus sp., Castanopsis acuminatissima, and members of the Myrtaceae, Elaeocarpaceae, Cunoniaceae, Lauraceae, Myrsinaceae and Euphorbiaceae are important. Nothofagus sp. dominates on some of the steeper limestone slopes to the north of the swamp, whereas Castanopsis acuminatissima forest are dominant in small patches on hilltops and near settlements. Below 1800 to 2000 m, regrowth shrubs occur within grassland. Species of Macaranga, Eurya, Ficus, Saurauia, Garcinia, Psychotria, and Acalypha are common in regrowth forest. Dodonaea forms monotypic stands of regrowth forest in some areas. Casuarina oligodon is commonly planted along the edge of gardens and around settlements and appears as a dominant plant in the landscape. Ischaemum polystachyum, Imperata cylindrica and Miscanthus floridulus dominate large areas of grassland. Gardens occur around the entire perimeter of the swamp and in some places extend out into the centre where periodic drainage of sections renders the swamp surface suitable for cultivation. The very wet areas of the swamp are dominated by Leersia hexandra short grass community. The sedges Schoenoplectus mucronatus and Machaerina rubignosa dominate towards the centre of  the swamp.
